_comment: Opt-in public alpha safety starter. Six command/canary rules; no workflow or conversational policy. Command matching is best-effort and does not replace backups, review, or branch protection.

rules.intent: recursive force-delete can destroy work irrecoverably
rules.message: recursive force-delete can destroy work irrecoverably

rules.intent: piping a download straight into a shell executes unreviewed remote code
rules.message: piping a download straight into a shell executes unreviewed remote code

rules.intent: force push can discard published history for everyone
rules.message: force push can discard published history for everyone

rules.intent: hard reset / clean -fd discards uncommitted work with no undo
rules.message: hard reset / clean -fd discards uncommitted work with no undo

rules.intent: linking this device to a team server is a new capability: it decides where governed-session records and device reports go. So is adopting or publishing a shared bundle, making or using the organization key, trusting a new organization key, sending a session to a teammate, and turning memory recall on or off in a runtime's settings. An agent following an injected instruction would use these verbs; a person confirms. A tripwire, not a wall — a process that writes the link files directly bypasses it, and the daemon then detects the drift.
rules.message: this changes what this device shares with a team server, trusts from it, sends a teammate, or writes into a runtime's settings for memory recall — confirm it is you
rules.backstop: the daemon refuses to re-link while linked, chains every link change, and flags files changed behind its back

rules.intent: the proof mechanism: demo and hook verification send this marker through the real hook; deleting it disables the demo only
rules.message: canary blocked — enforcement is live (this is the verification marker, not a real command)
